S18.user_text: This is the right-hand side of the Green's function's equation of motion — the step that is written across into the sister scenario. The sign is for $[\hat H,\hat c]$; $[\hat c,\hat H]$ is its negative.

S19.user_text: **From here on the time-carrying operator itself is the object** (PAIR-REP, docs/34 §2). $\hat c(t)=e^{i\hat Ht}\hat ce^{-i\hat Ht}$ is not a new kind of quantity but the sum of nested commutators $\sum_n (it)^n/n!\,\mathrm{ad}_H^n(\hat c)$. With a diagonal $\hat H_0$, $[\hat H_0,\hat c_m]=-\varepsilon_m\hat c_m$ closes on ONE operator, so the sum resums into an exponential **exactly** — this is not a truncation.

S29.user_text: **The different-time anticommutator.** This is what the representation is for: $\{\hat c_m(t),\hat c^\dagger_m(u)\}=f(t)\overline{f(u)}\{\hat c_m,\hat c^\dagger_m\}$ — coefficient product times equal-time algebra. Folding time into an index would have collapsed it to $\delta(t,u)$. The equal-time $\{\hat c,\hat c^\dagger\}=1$ cancels and what remains is a SCALAR with no operator in it: the time dependence of the free propagator.
